entries.title: What is ibogaine, and why is it in the news?
entries.summary: Public-radio segment with pharmacologist Deborah Mash and Microdose journalist Jane Hu on ibogaine’s research history, recent U.S. policy attention, and how it sits inside broader psychedelic medicine coverage. Mash’s company role is disclosed on-air; treat efficacy framing as media, not trial evidence.
entries.notes: Companion show page (also 200): https://www.sciencefriday.com/segments/ibogaine-psychadelics/ — note official slug spelling psychadelics.

entries.title: Ibogaine for Addiction: What the Science Says About Treatment, Safety & the Future of Psychedelic Medicine | Dr. Deborah Mash
entries.summary: Long-form researcher interview with Deborah Mash on addiction-interruption research history, safety themes, noribogaine interest, and adjacent neurology questions. Company/developer role is relevant conflict context; keep medical claims labeled media until primary-sourced.

entries.title: Episode 859: Ibogaine – The Science Behind How It Works
entries.summary: Stanford psychiatrist Nolan Williams discusses magnesium–ibogaine observational work in veterans with TBI, cardiac-risk mitigation themes, and research pathway talk. Distinct from Newt’s World 858/872/902 already catalogued. Pair efficacy percentages with the primary Nature Medicine paper — media paraphrase is not the trial record.

entries.title: Ibogaine and the Future of Healing: Trevor Millar & Jonathan Dickinson of Ambio Life Sciences
entries.summary: Interview with Ambio leaders on addiction/neuroregeneration framing, safety/ethics, and scaling questions ahead of Psychedelic Science 2025. Clinic-proximate guests — catalog for claim themes and culture/ethics talk; IbogaBase does not refer listeners to clinics.
entries.notes: Commercial-proximity awareness (Ambio). Omit clinic referral language in IbogaBase voice.

entries.title: Iboga Initiation and the Wisdom of Discomfort — Paije Alexandra West
entries.summary: Conversation on Bwiti initiation context, root bark versus total-alkaloid extract distinctions as discussed in media, and why ceremony/community framing differs from clinic-only alkaloid models. Guest is a retreat founder — clinic/retreat-proximate; keep as culture/media literacy, not a referral.
entries.notes: datePublished 2026-09-07 from Third Wave page JSON-LD. Commercial/retreat-proximity awareness (ETÉREO). No dosing detail reproduced.

entries.title: Ibogaine Inquiries Part I: Remember the Name
entries.summary: Series opener tracing how ibogaine moved from Gabonese ceremonial contexts into U.S. veteran/advocacy and policy conversation after high-profile executive-order coverage. High-reach explainer; advocacy guests overstate efficacy at times — claim-check against primary sources.
entries.notes: Official series page hub: https://thetelepathytapes.com/podcast (GET 200). Series includes Parts I–V; Parts II/IV not separately shelved this pass.

entries.title: Ibogaine Inquiries Part III: The Sacred Roots of Iboga
entries.summary: Culture/stewardship-focused episode on Gabonese Bwiti contexts and Blessings of the Forest conservation framing with Yann Guignon. Useful media literacy for indigenous-source pressure; IbogaBase does not reproduce sacred ritual instructions.
entries.notes: No sacred ritual detail copied into IbogaBase summaries.

entries.title: Ibogaine Inquiries Part V: Before the Forest Is Gone
entries.summary: Conservation and commodification closer: wild harvest pressure, rising prices, and risks when ceremonies spread faster than stewardship capacity. Pair with culture-stewardship reference pages; treat as media advocacy, not a primary ecological survey.
entries.notes: Series ender; Blessings of the Forest org mentioned in episode notes — not a clinic referral.
